note: A delivery statement refuses rather than guesses. Each entry's blocker is the code its replaced test asserts: ambiguous_documented_column_identity (cannot_choose: blockers == that code; an 'ambiguous' blocker is reported over-broad), native_variable_id_not_documented_for_column (anchor_missing), now_present for a version the column is already delivered in (conversion_reports[now_present] and the present-column half of requires_anchor: blocker startswith 'now_present:'; the ':2020' suffix is the entry's version; test_addition_is_a_bounded_claim's reappearing-evidence half is the same refusal in a fresh build), unsupported_storage_header for a header with no storage row (storage_header[WRONG]). The detail format '<entry locator>: <blockers>' is how the compile reports a refused [[errata.delivered]] entry; it is kept as a field because it is the only boundary signal of the blocker code (the rows are selected by code alone). No refused entry adds a 2020 state (old: case is None): AMB, MISS and ADDW have no 2020 state at all, and NOW and ADDN keep only their delivered 2020 state, none with an errata provenance (an applied [[errata.delivered]] state's provenance starts 'errata:', as in errata-delivered-simultaneous-components-are-added-beside-the-blank-native-base). Allowed twins: errata-delivered-additional-physical-column-keeps-its-siblings (anchored additional deliveries with an exact storage header apply) and errata-delivered-statement-types-widen-documentation-and-storage (ANC: an anchor that selects one documented identity applies).
fails_if: `scb_errata.convert_delivered_entry` picks one of several documented native variables instead of refusing, accepts an anchor no documented row carries, adds a column to a version that already delivers it, or ignores an explicit storage header without a storage row; each turns one of the five refusal rows into an applied entry
